# Blocking defects in the training and education chain, with proposed textual fixes

**Rule:** proposed 7.35.3 NMAC as published July 23, 2026. `docs/documents/rules-draft-2026-07-23-published.pdf`. Rule hearing August 28, 2026.

**Relationship to the other files in this folder.** `metz-crosswalk.md` maps the July 17 recommendations against the published text. `7.35.3.18-19-redline.md` carries the amendment language for 7.35.3.18 and 7.35.3.19. This file carries the defects that block the training and education chain, and the amendment language for the two provisions outside those sections that the redline depends on: 7.35.3.14 and 7.35.3.20 (H)(5).

**Ordering.** Defect 1 is first because it is the one that stops the practicum from being lawful rather than merely difficult. The remaining defects follow the numbering in `analysis/july23-rule-concerns.md` so the two documents can be read side by side.

**Conventions.** Page citations are to the printed page of the published PDF. Rule quotations are verbatim from its text layer with PDF line breaks collapsed to single spaces and no other alteration. Both July 17 transcripts are labeled "UNOFFICIAL AUTO-GENERATED TRANSCRIPT. NO SPEAKER ATTRIBUTION"; a speaker is named only where the surrounding transcript text fixes it and the basis is stated. The permit title is carried as the variable described in `7.35.3.18-19-redline.md`; the rendered copy of this file is `blocking-defects-rendered.md`. Quotations never carry the variable: where a quotation contains the permit title, the title is reproduced literally as it appears in the source.

## Defect 1. The rule requires students to conduct supervised facilitation and does not authorize a student to possess or administer psilocybin

**Sections 7.35.3.14 (page 9), 7.35.3.19 A (pages 12 and 13), 7.35.3.20 D and H(5) (page 14). Both 7.35.3.14 and the "qualified student" clause are new text with no counterpart in the July 9 draft.** Corresponds to B1 in `analysis/july23-rule-concerns.md`.

### 1.1 The three provisions

7.35.3.14 is framed as the authorization provision, and its heading names the categories exhaustively:

> "7.34.3.14 AUTHORIZED POSSESSION, PURCHASE, OR SALE OF MEDICAL PSILOCYBIN BY PRACTITIONERS, FACILITATORS, HEALING CENTER OWNERS AND EMPLOYEES: Certification of a practitioner, facilitator, or healing center shall enable practitioners, facilitators, and owners and employees of healing centers to do the following, in accordance with medical psilocybin program rules:"

Its three subsections grant possession and administration authority to practitioners, to facilitators, and to "Owners and employees of healing centers who are registered with the department". Students appear nowhere in the section.

7.35.3.19 A requires students to do the work:

> "Students shall participate in a minimum of 80 hours of administration day sessions, where students are provided the opportunity to experience, observe, or conduct supervised facilitation of administration day sessions in-person with a minimum of 14 different patients over a minimum of eight different administration and same-day sessions"

7.35.3.20 H(5) counts students toward mandatory staffing:

> "in group administration sessions a minimum of one practitioner for every eight patients and a minimum of one facilitator or qualified student for every two patients. For purposes of the foregoing provision, a student shall be deemed qualified if they are registered with a certified educational program and they have completed at least 50 hours of their practicum."

### 1.2 Why this is blocking and not a drafting preference

A student who conducts supervised facilitation, or who fills one of the required staffing positions, will handle psilocybin product. 7.35.3.14 is the provision that performs the authorizing function for every other category of person in the room, and it does not reach students. A practicum student holds no certification, which is the thing the practicum is a prerequisite for: 7.35.3.19 A requires the practicum to be "completed prior to applying for certification."

7.35.3.22, page 15, then provides that participation in the program "does not relieve the qualified patient or certificant from criminal prosecution or civil penalties for ... Unlawful distribution, transfer, or use of psilocybin." A student is neither a qualified patient nor a certificant, so the class the sentence addresses does not include the person the practicum puts in the room with the medicine.

A student who is separately employed by a healing center might be reached through 7.35.3.14 (C), but that is a property of some students rather than a rule about students, and the practicum requirement does not depend on it. Defect 2 below shows that the (C) route does not presently work either.

### 1.3 What the July 17 record shows

The intent is not in doubt. At the July 17 afternoon Training and Education Committee meeting the department described the practicum as including facilitation by students. The transcript fixes the speaker: the chair says "Thank you for explaining that, Dominic" at the end of the same passage.

> "Talking about the practicum we have in the proposed rules that we had shared is that it includes the ability for those students to not just observe, but also to be facilitating, for example, or acting in the practitioner role. And so that's already in there."

The same meeting records the response to the proposed training permit, from the same speaker in a later passage that opens "I see Dominic's hand up":

> "that really wouldn't be necessary with the model that we have and the way that we put the practitioner aspect in there. Just because that already would be covered as them being a registered student with an educational program where they have that ability to be a part of those training sessions, including to conduct them under supervision"

> "those students already will have that kind of protection ability to be there as a part of being registered as a student with an educational program"

The published text contains no provision that produces that coverage. Registration with an educational program appears in the published rule in exactly two places, 7.35.3.20 D and 7.35.3.20 H(5), and neither confers possession or administration authority. 7.35.3.20 D confers presence only:

> "Except in circumstances involving an emergency response, only patients, certified individuals, and students completing their practicums may be present during an administration session unless each patient gives prior written consent for the other individual(s) to be present."

The staffing-ratio suggestion from the same meeting was implemented within six days. The transcript records the department taking it back for review: "we can definitely take a look at that if that would be after they've completed so many hours to be a part of that rather than needing to create an entire other permit or certification level. But we could definitely look at that. I'll take that on back as well." 7.35.3.20 H(5) adopts it with a 50-hour threshold. The authorization that the same exchange said was unnecessary was not added. That is the sequence that turns this from an omission into a defect: the rule now requires the conduct in two places and authorizes it in none.

The need for a permit was also stated at the meeting by a committee participant, in permit terms:

> "I do really like this permit, like the training permit. model, but that would require incorporation within regulations. So it's a new permit type, whether we call it a training permit or a practitioner in training permit or some other name, it would be a new permit type."

> "I do think it's important that it have a DOH permit designation because I think what's key to the affordability part of that model is that person can count as one of the two practitioners that's required under other sections of the department regulations."

### 1.4 Proposed fix, part one: 7.35.3.14

Redline key: **bold** is inserted, ~~strikethrough~~ is deleted.

> ~~7.34.3.14~~ **7.35.3.14** AUTHORIZED POSSESSION, PURCHASE, OR SALE OF MEDICAL PSILOCYBIN BY PRACTITIONERS, FACILITATORS, **TRAINING PERMITTEES,** HEALING CENTER OWNERS AND EMPLOYEES: Certification of a practitioner, facilitator, or healing center**, and issuance of a training permit under Subsection H of 7.35.3.19 NMAC,** shall enable practitioners, facilitators, **training permittees,** and owners and employees of healing centers to do the following, in accordance with medical psilocybin program rules:
>
> ~~(A)~~ **A.** Practitioners: [text unchanged]
>
> ~~(B)~~ **B.** Facilitators: [text unchanged]
>
> ~~(C)~~ **C.** Healing centers: Owners and employees of healing centers who are ~~registered with the department~~ **designated to the department by the healing center in accordance with Subsection M of 7.35.3.20 NMAC** may purchase medical psilocybin products from permitted producers, may possess medical psilocybin products, and may sell or otherwise administer those products to qualified patients in administration sessions conducted at the healing center or other approved locations, provided that such individuals are also designated to engage in each activity by the healing center. A healing center may only sell or otherwise provide psilocybin products that are obtained from permitted producers.
>
> **D. Training permittees: A student who holds a current training permit issued under Subsection H of 7.35.3.19 NMAC may possess medical psilocybin products, and may administer or otherwise provide those products to qualified patients in administration sessions conducted at a healing center or other approved location, in each case only while under the direct, on-site supervision of a practicum supervisor registered under Subsection F of 7.35.3.19 NMAC, and only to the extent required by the practicum under 7.35.3.19 NMAC. A training permittee shall not purchase medical psilocybin products.**

Three notes on the drafting.

The section-number correction from 7.34.3.14 to 7.35.3.14 is mechanical. The heading as published points at Chapter 34 of Title 7, which is a different chapter, while the bracketed history note at the end of the same section reads "[7.35.3.14 NMAC, xx/xx/2026]". Four other headings carry the same error; the complete list is at `analysis/july23-rule-concerns.md`, N1.

The subsection letters are changed from "(A)", "(B)", "(C)" to "A.", "B.", "C." to match the style used in every other section of the rule. 7.35.3.11 A carries the same anomaly. Recorded at `analysis/july23-rule-concerns.md`, N4.

Subsection D grants possession and administration but withholds purchase. A training permittee has no reason to buy product, and withholding it keeps the chain of custody with a certificant.

### 1.5 Proposed fix, part two: the permit itself

The permit is created at new 7.35.3.19 H. Full text is in `7.35.3.18-19-redline.md`, Subsection H. In outline: issuance on completion of stage one of the practicum sequence plus the same life-support, HIPAA and sex-offender attestation items the certification application requires; a 30-day decision deadline with a right of appeal; authority conferred by cross-reference to 7.35.3.14; a 24-month term renewable once for 12 months; expiry on certification or on ceasing to be a registered student; and a statement that a training permittee is a certificant for purposes of the rule.

### 1.6 Proposed fix, part three: 7.35.3.20 (H)(5)

> (5) Includes procedures to ensure that there are practitioners and facilitators present at all times during an administration session with a minimum of one practitioner and one facilitator for individual patient sessions; and in group administration sessions a minimum of one practitioner for every eight patients and a minimum of one facilitator or qualified student for every two patients. For purposes of the foregoing provision, a student shall be deemed qualified if they ~~are registered with a certified educational program and they have completed at least 50 hours of their practicum~~ **hold a current training permit issued under Subsection H of 7.35.3.19 NMAC and have completed at least 50 hours of their practicum. Qualified students shall not fill more than half of the facilitator positions required by this paragraph in any administration session, and a session staffed in part by qualified students shall include at least one certified facilitator.** Exception: the department may waive or decrease this ratio if the department determines that the ratio specified presents a barrier for patients and that safety concerns are otherwise alleviated.

Two changes.

The first substitutes the training permit for bare registration with an educational program as the qualifying condition. This is what makes the paragraph consistent with 7.35.3.14 as amended: a person counted toward mandatory staffing in a session where psilocybin is administered is a person authorized to handle it. The 50-hour threshold is retained, so the paragraph continues to implement what was taken back for review on July 17 in the terms it was taken back: "if that would be after they've completed so many hours to be a part of that."

The second caps substitution. As published, a group session of eight patients requires four facilitator positions and every one of them may be filled by a student who has logged 50 practicum hours, under a single practitioner who is simultaneously responsible for all eight patients. The cap keeps at least one certified facilitator in the room and limits students to half the required positions. This also narrows the conflict recorded at `analysis/july23-rule-concerns.md`, M15, between the staffing ratio and the "direct supervision" requirement in 7.35.3.13 B.

The section-number correction from 7.34.3.20 to 7.35.3.20 applies to this section's heading as well.

### 1.7 Conforming amendment outside this scope

7.35.3.22, page 15, addresses "the qualified patient or certificant". 7.35.3.19 H(5) as drafted states that a training permittee is a certificant for purposes of the rule, which should be sufficient. An express addition to 7.35.3.22 would remove any doubt. Flagged, not drafted. See `metz-crosswalk.md`, flag F2.

## Defect 2. Healing center owners and employees are authorized only if registered with the department, and no registration exists

**Section 7.35.3.14 (C), page 9. New text.** Corresponds to B5 in `analysis/july23-rule-concerns.md`.

> "(C) Healing centers: Owners and employees of healing centers who are registered with the department may purchase medical psilocybin products from permitted producers, may possess medical psilocybin products, and may sell or otherwise administer those products to qualified patients"

The rule creates no registration process for healing center owners or employees. 7.35.3.11 A(11), page 5, requires an applicant healing center to submit "A list of all owners or members of the board of directors, including corresponding contact information", and A(2) requires "Names and contact information of primary contact person(s) and any affiliated practitioners or facilitators". Neither is described as registration, and neither covers employees generally. As written, the condition precedent to lawful possession by healing center staff cannot be satisfied.

This defect sits in the same section as Defect 1 and has to be fixed alongside it, because the (C) route is the only route by which a practicum student who happens to be a healing center employee could be covered under the published rule.

**Proposed fix.** Two parts. The first is the amendment to 7.35.3.14 (C) in section 1.4 above, which replaces "registered with the department" with a designation made by the healing center. The second is a new subsection in 7.35.3.20 creating the designation. 7.35.3.20 currently runs A through L, so the new subsection is M:

> **M. Designation of owners and employees: A healing center shall submit to the department, through the electronic system designated by the department, a current list of the owners and employees the healing center designates to purchase, possess, sell or administer medical psilocybin products, identifying which of those activities each designated individual is authorized to engage in. A healing center shall update the list within five business days of a change. An individual is designated for purposes of Subsection C of 7.35.3.14 NMAC on submission of the list identifying them.**

7.35.3.20 is in scope only at H(5) by the terms of this drafting assignment. Subsection M is offered because Defect 2 cannot be fixed inside 7.35.3.14 alone: the section can name a mechanism but cannot create one. If the addition of 7.35.3.20 M is not wanted, the alternative is to strike "who are registered with the department" from 7.35.3.14 (C) and rely on the designation requirement already in the subsection's own closing clause, "provided that such individuals are also designated to engage in each activity by the healing center." That alternative is shorter and leaves the department without a list.

## Defect 3. The New Mexico module gates every pathway and has no delivery date

**Section 7.35.3.18 A, page 11. Carried over from the July 9 draft.** Corresponds to B2 in `analysis/july23-rule-concerns.md`.

> "All certifying clinicians, practitioners, and facilitators who provide medical psilocybin services, including all such providers who are certified by the department on the basis of having completed an educational program from another jurisdiction, shall complete a New Mexico educational module created or approved by the department prior to applying for certification"

7.35.3.10 B(3), page 4, repeats the requirement for out-of-jurisdiction applicants. 7.35.3.17 B, page 11, carves the New Mexico module out of the test-out option, so no one may bypass it. The rule imposes no deadline on the department to create or approve the module, no requirement that it be published, and no hour count, although every other module in 7.35.3.18 carries an hour minimum.

The July 17 afternoon committee agenda as read into the record included the open question "Reciprocity, when will the New Mexico modules be available for reciprocity?" The transcript contains no answer.

**Proposed fix.** Drafted at `7.35.3.18-19-redline.md`, Subsections A and I: an eight-hour minimum, a 90-day publication deadline binding the department, and a rule that an applicant is not denied certification on the ground that the module was unavailable and completes it within 90 days of publication.

**In scope.** Yes, 7.35.3.18.

## Defect 4. The practicum cannot be performed at launch, and the only relief is a standardless waiver

**Sections 7.35.3.19 A and D, pages 12 and 13. Hours carried over; the entry gate is new.** Corresponds to B4 in `analysis/july23-rule-concerns.md`.

The chain: each student needs 14 different qualified patients across at least eight administration day sessions, including two group sessions with four or more patients each. Those hours must occur at an approved healing center or other approved location, because 7.35.3.19 D provides that "All practicum hours shall take place in an approved healing center or other approved location." Other approved locations are available only in the circumstances set out in 7.35.3.11 B, page 6, and are certified for 90 days. Nothing authorizes practicum with participants who are not qualified patients. So the practicum supply is bounded by the enrolled patient population, which requires certifying clinicians, which requires the New Mexico module, which is Defect 3.

Both halves were raised on July 17 at the afternoon committee meeting. On placement: "the current draft requires that all hours be held in an approved healing center, which I think can potentially be a bottleneck for rural trainees," with the proposed remedy "the apprenticeship or the site supervisor model, similar to what they do for counseling licensure or direct entry midwifery." On patient supply: "The current indications really limit our patient pool and therefore placements and trainees getting through it," and a proposal that practicum "be operated on well patients, those without qualifying conditions." The morning board transcript records the statutory version of the same point: "what's going to be presented in the training committee this afternoon is impossible to do adequate training without having the ability for people to use psilocybin in the training."

The only relief in the published rule is two discretionary waivers with no criteria, no procedure, and no time limit, at 7.35.3.10 D(2), page 5, and 7.35.3.19 F, page 13, both reading in substance:

> "The department may otherwise waive, temporarily suspend, or reduce the practicum requirements for individuals applying for certification, in order to facilitate the certification of individuals trained by other government-approved programs, and to build the initial infrastructure of the program."

**Proposed fix, the part that is drafted.** Three amendments in `7.35.3.18-19-redline.md`: Subsection E permits a healing center or other approved location to host a student whose program is not co-located; new Subsection F creates a registered practicum supervisor with published lists of supervisors and available sites; Subsection K adds a 30-day decision deadline, a written basis, a 40-hour contact-time floor, a bar on waiving the consultation requirement, a bar on authorizing an unpermitted person to handle product, and annual publication of waivers granted.

**The part that is not drafted, and cannot be.** Practicum with participants who are not qualified patients. Nothing in 7.35.3 NMAC authorizes administering psilocybin outside the medical program, and the department cannot supply that authority by rule. This is set out at `metz-crosswalk.md`, Part 4.4. It is the reason the redline builds the risk gradient from role rather than from participant status.

**In scope.** The drafted parts, yes, all in 7.35.3.19.

## Defect 5. The third-party evaluator conflict rule disqualifies the evaluators the program must hire

**Section 7.35.3.16 A and C(2)(b), page 10. Carried over from the July 9 draft.** Corresponds to B3 in `analysis/july23-rule-concerns.md`.

> "A. General requirements: A psilocybin educational program shall engage a qualified third-party evaluation team to conduct the evaluations required under this rule."

> "(b) Holding a financial interest in, receiving compensation from, or serving in any governance or advisory capacity with the program or organization being evaluated."

Subsection A obliges the program to engage the team, which means the program pays it. Subsection C(2)(b) makes "receiving compensation from ... the program or organization being evaluated" a disqualifying conflict with no carve-out for the evaluation fee itself. Read as written, no person can lawfully serve. 7.35.3.12 A(20), page 7, makes the resulting report a required component of a complete application, so the defect propagates to every educational program application.

**Proposed fix, not drafted here.** One clause: insert at the end of C(2)(b) "; provided that a fee paid for the evaluation engagement itself is not compensation for purposes of this subparagraph". 7.35.3.16 is outside this drafting scope. Recorded here so that the list of blocking defects in the training and education chain is complete.

**In scope.** No.

## Order of dependency

If the amendments are taken in pieces, this is the order in which they have to be taken for each piece to have anything to operate on.

1. **7.35.3.14 D and 7.35.3.19 H, together.** Neither works alone. 7.35.3.14 D authorizes a permit that 7.35.3.19 H creates; 7.35.3.19 H issues a permit whose content is stated in 7.35.3.14 D.
2. **7.35.3.20 H(5).** Depends on 1. Without the permit, substituting "holds a current training permit" for the 50-hour test would empty the paragraph.
3. **7.35.3.19 D, the practicum sequence.** Depends on 1, because stage two requires a training permit.
4. **7.35.3.19 E and F, location and supervisors.** Independent of 1, and independently useful.
5. **7.35.3.18, the didactic amendments.** Independent of all of the above.
6. **7.35.3.19 I and J, consultation and the end-of-life checkpoint.** I depends on 1 for the phrase "during the training permit period"; if the permit is not adopted, I can be restated as running from the completion of the practicum, which is where 7.35.3.17 A currently places the mentoring.

The hours proposal in `7.35.3.18-19-redline.md` stands or falls as a unit: the practicum reduction at 7.35.3.19 A and C is offered together with the didactic increase at 7.35.3.18 C and H and the consultation increase at 7.35.3.19 I. Adopting the practicum reduction alone would lower the program total, which is not what is proposed. See `metz-crosswalk.md`, Part 6.
